subject: Dedicated capacity incident: customer runbook & risk mitigation
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hansen <tom.hansen@blueriver.ai>
Cc: Sara Vance <sara.vance@blueriver.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 21:14:00 +0000
Subject: Dedicated capacity — noticed degraded throughput on your pool

Hi Tom / Sara,

We’re flagging a transient degradation in throughput from the dedicated GPU pool backing your production cluster (pool: br-2093-prod). Our observability detected an increase in tail latency and queueing between 20:50–21:05 UTC; this impacted short tail calls and caused occasional request retries in your fleet.

What we’ve done so far:
- Ingested metrics and traces into the incident dashboard (link below).
- Pinned the pool to warm-standby mode to limit eviction cycles.
- Kicked off an autoscaler health check and a targeted warm-node allocation (in progress).

Immediate impact: 5–8% request latency increase for brief bursts; no data loss or cross-tenant leakage.

We’ll keep you updated with concrete timings for remediation. Expect the next note in ~30–45 minutes; I’m also looped in with Marcus (SRE lead) and Monica (CS) to coordinate.

Apologies for the disruption — we know this affects your live traffic patterns during your peak window.

Quick links: incident dashboard: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-8321

Best,
Soojin Lee

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 00:03:08 +0000
Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated capacity — noticed degraded throughput on your pool

Soojin / team — quick update from SRE triage:

What we found:
- Root cause (preliminary): rapid autoscaler backoff interacting with node eviction heuristics for high-burst traffic patterns. The first-order failure mode is short-lived KV-cache rehydration + queue saturation while the pool re-warms.
- A small subset of jobs experienced request queueing while nodes were evicted and reattached.

Immediate mitigations applied (30m window):
1) Forced warm-standby allocation for br-2093-prod (added 2 × p4d warm nodes).
2) Increased autoscaler cooldown to 120s to avoid thrash during bursts.
3) Enabled targeted prefix-KV caching for BlueRiver’s model family to limit rehydration time.

Customer-facing runbook (attached): incident_runbook_v3.pdf — 1 page, includes recommended client-side throttles, retry/backoff guidance, and a contact matrix.

Follow-ups / next steps:
- We’ll push a small autoscaler patch to avoid immediate backoff regressions (autoscale_patch.diff) during low-latency bursts; ETA: 14:00 UTC tomorrow (2026-10-01).
- Post-incident: full postmortem with timelines and permanent remediation plan within 72 hours.
- Propose a one-time SLA credit for the impacted window; Monica, can you prepare the credit amount and customer comms?

I’ll keep monitoring and will post status to INF-8321.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
SRE Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Tom Hansen <tom.hansen@blueriver.ai>, Sara Vance <sara.vance@blueriver.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Sep 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — customer runbook & mitigation summary

Hi Tom / Sara — final update for the incident window earlier this evening.

Summary:
- What happened: temporary throughput degradation in your reserved GPU pool (br-2093-prod) caused by an interaction between autoscaler backoff and eviction heuristics; this produced short-lived queueing while nodes warmed.
- What we did: applied warm-standby nodes, increased autoscaler cooldown, and enabled targeted prefix-KV caching. We attached a short runbook and guidance for your ops team.
- Current state: nominal — metrics have returned to baseline and no further retries observed since ~16:20 UTC.

Attached items: incident_runbook_v3.pdf (customer runbook), autoscale_patch.diff (engineering patch for later rollout).

Compensation and next steps:
- Monica will follow up with a proposed SLA credit for the impacted window and a brief note regarding how we calculated the credit.
- Engineering will schedule the autoscaler patch for 2026-10-01 (14:00 UTC) with a canary rollout.
- We’ll publish a detailed postmortem (INF-8321) within 72 hours that includes timeline, root cause, and permanent mitigations.

Action for BlueRiver ops: please review the attached runbook and confirm if you want us to add it to your on-call playbook (we can push to your GitHub/Confluence). If you approve the runbook, Monica will also issue the SLA credit via the DocuSign link (https://www.docusign.com/en/link/BR-2093-credit-approval) for signature.

Thank you for your patience; appreciate the quick signal from your team — that helped us prioritize the warm-node allocation. If any regressions appear, ping me directly and we’ll escalate immediately.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
